scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

estimate substitution when no accepted read

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-REQUESTER-FRAMING.statement: The requester's framing is correct: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

H-ROOT-CAUSE-UNKNOWN.statement: The operational root cause differs from the requested solution and must be established from data

interpretation_history.interpretation: The dispute ticket volume rose from about 600 in June/July to roughly 1180-1260 in August‑September, approximately doubling since August.
The tariff change log contains no records, indicating that no tariff changes have been logged in the billing system during the period under review.

The observation shows disputed bills for both estimated (1240) and actual (1785) reads, with actual reads higher, indicating that the dispute surge is not limited to estimated reads and points to broader billing issues.
The median dispute response time is 1.6 days, well within the SLA of 3.0 days, indicating that response latency is not a likely driver of the dispute surge.

Route completion for August‑September is 0.88 (88%) against a target of 0.95, with 9,200 manual read accounts, indicating field manual read coverage is below target and may contribute to billing disputes.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder’s statement that there has been no tariff change this year indicates that tariff changes are unlikely to be driving the dispute surge.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Shortage of three field readers since July has caused routes to run late, leading to estimated bills for affected customers.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that the utility can request route priority changes, but such changes require confirmation by the Field Operations Manager, reinforcing the existing dispatch approval process.
